- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce the slope of the forecast to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (0.00) and forecast is rising, cap the forecast at the 3rd-to-last true value to avoid false momentum.  
- If the last 3 true values show a sharp spike (≥10% from prior), reduce forecast slope by 15–20% to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast is consistently above true values for 5+ days, apply mean reversion by subtracting 0.5–1.0 from the forecasted value per day.  
- If forecast is below true values for 5+ days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0 per day to catch up.  
- For horizon > 10 days, reduce forecast slope if sentiment is flat or negative to avoid drift.  
- If sentiment is 0.00 and true values show a clear downward trend, forecast should not rise above the 2nd-to-last true value.
